_about: Life satisfaction for the National mood section, hand-filed from primary reports. Every mean retains its survey's own scale, sample and panel; nothing is pooled, lean-adjusted or rescaled. Readings with only a year sit at mid-year. `quote` is the verbatim source sentence or table text proving that reading; `source` identifies it. DemosAU's separate 0–100 snapshot is derived from demosau-one-offs.json by gen-data, not duplicated here.

series.question: Overall, how satisfied are you with life as a whole these days?
series.answers: 0 means not at all satisfied and 10 means completely satisfied.
series.method: ANUpoll’s national adult mean, not the ABS/HILDA series. The probability-recruited Life in Australia panel ran until January 2024; the opt-in ORU online panel began in October 2024. The empty months are intentional: only waves whose exact means appear in a primary text are filed, never values eyeballed from ANU’s image-only trend chart.

readings.quote: Average life satisfaction reached a then-low of 6.52 in April 2020, fluctuated during the COVID-19 pandemic, and rose back to 6.78 by January 2023.

series.question: All things considered, how satisfied are you with your life?
series.answers: 0 to 10, where 0 means not at all satisfied and 10 completely satisfied.
series.method: Annual Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia Survey readings, printed to one decimal in the ABS’s custom analysis. HILDA tracks the same households over time rather than taking a fresh ANUpoll sample; 2014–2023 is the run published on this ABS table, not the complete HILDA history.

series.question: Overall, on a scale from 0 to 10, how satisfied are you with life as a whole these days?
series.answers: 0 means not at all satisfied and 10 completely satisfied.
series.method: The ABS General Social Survey, Australians aged 15 and over. Only 2014, 2019, 2020 and 2025 are printed here. The 2020 survey moved from face-to-face to online and telephone interviewing during COVID-19, which the ABS says may have affected comparisons; 2025 fieldwork was in May and June.

series.question: Respondents ranked their overall life satisfaction on a scale of 0 to 10.
series.answers: 0 to 10; the report prints the national mean and the share giving each score band, not a categorical satisfied share.
series.method: The 2024 Mapping Social Cohesion survey, 7,965 adults in July 2024, 99% online and 1% by telephone through the probability-recruited Life in Australia panel. This is Scanlon’s own reading, not the ABS figures its reports also quote.

readings.quote: In 2024, survey respondents were also asked to rank their overall life satisfaction on a scale of 0 to 10. The average score respondents gave was 6.8.
